Founded in 2000 as a student project, BRV fund managers source new investment opportunities, conduct opportunity assessments and due diligence, make investment recommendations, assess and vote on recommendations of other fund managers, and make investments in early-stage, high-growth startup companies. Fund managers also manage existing portfolio investments, conduct annual portfolio valuations, and prepare investor materials such as an annual report and annual meeting. Fund managers operate under the guidance and oversight of experienced practitioner faculty. BRV is a selective program, with an application and interview process open to MBAs, JDs, and PhD candidates; the course is only open to students who apply to become and are selected as fund managers (see brventurefund.com for application details and timing). Full participation at either the Ithaca or Cornell Tech campuses, both fall and spring semester, is required. (MHA-EL)
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Fall 2026 NBA 5075 distance learning students

classes.subject: NBA
classes.title: Dilemmas in Founding New Ventures
classes.description: The purpose of NBA5645 Dilemmas in Founding New Ventures is to increase your startup's chances of success by helping you avoid the #1 reason for startup failure: not strategy, not product, not execution, but TEAM-related mistakes. We start by analyzing the very first decision in any new venture, whether to found solo or with others. If you have co-founders, who will they be? And how will you split the equity? Finally, we wrestle with the fundamental tradeoff in entrepreneurship: Growth vs. Glory. Can you grow your startup quickly without being replaced by a seasoned CEO? I'll teach you techniques for keeping control, which too many founders realize too late they have lost. For further information, please visit: http://nba5645.org. (MHA-EL)
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Johnson Cornell Tech Master of Business Administration (MBA); others by permission of instructor
classes.grading_summary: Participation 35, pre-class polls 15, business model analysis 25, founders' agreement 25; no exam in SP26

classes.subject: NBA
classes.title: Customer Analytics and Strategy
classes.description: The course is aimed at students who are interested in pursuing activities in customer strategy and analytics built around the notion of customer centricity. The primary objective of this course is to provide students how customer management can help accomplish strategic initiatives, improve firm profitability and build lasting competitive advantage. Students will be exposed to the practical side of customer management through case studies and hands-on exercises. This course is particularly relevant for students interested in careers in consulting, product, service and brand management, and retailing as well as for entrepreneurs. (MHA-EL)

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Introduction to Finance Analytics
classes.description: The purpose of this course is to give students a broad understanding of how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can be used in financial analysis and decision-making. The emphasis is on helping students understand and apply modern analytical tools to extract information from financial data, identify patterns, generate predictions, and support investment and business decisions. The course format is a combination of examples, case studies, lectures, and hands-on applications. Potential topics include financial data sources, machine learning methods for financial prediction, natural language processing of financial documents and news, sentiment analysis, large language models (LLMs), financial forecasting, risk assessment, and AI-driven investment strategies. The course also examines the opportunities and limitations of AI and ML in financial applications, including issues of reliability, interpretability, and decision-making under uncertainty.

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Design Thinking
classes.description: In today's business landscape, creative problem solving has become a critical tool for leaders to drive innovation and transformation across different industries. Design has rapidly emerged as a driver for innovation, organizational change, and growth. Design Thinking has been adopted by major consulting firms, large corporations, tech start-ups, and NGOs. The course offers an opportunity to learn, practice, and enhance design skills through a 'deep dive.' Structured around project-based teamwork, fostering collaboration is crucial. Students focus on exploring human-centered innovation using clear, hands-on frameworks. With support from selected readings, case studies, and insights from guest speakers across various industries, the course ensures a comprehensive understanding of design and innovation thinking and methods.
classes.grading_summary: Pass/fail on completing all six deliverables (3 team, 3 individual); no weights

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: SMARTech Weekends (Strategy for Media, Art, Retail Technology)
classes.description: This course is for future leaders who understand that technology decisions in media, art, and retail ripple far beyond balance sheets. We will examine how digital technologies are transforming media, art, and retail —industries that don't just drive economic value, but fundamentally shape how we experience the world, express identity, and connect with one another. Students will analyze and understand the strategic implications of emerging technologies in these sectors and the opportunities and challenges they create at the intersection of culture and commerce. The course combines rigorous case analysis to derive conceptual frameworks – drawing from the case studies written by the instructor – with hands-on fieldwork, projects and insights from industry speakers. This course is ideal for students interested in entrepreneurship, strategy, or leadership roles where business decisions carry cultural weight. Whether you aspire to launch a creative venture, lead innovation at an established brand, or advise these industries through consulting or investing, you'll gain frameworks for navigating the complex intersection of technology, culture, and commerce.
classes.grading_summary: Project report 50, class participation 50; missing more than 2 sessions drops grade a third of a letter

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: FinTech Ecosystem Weekends
classes.description: The goal of the Fintech Intensive is to immerse students in the emerging Financial Technology sector.  We will explore the landscape, analyze past moves, discuss current trends, and identify future opportunities, while discussing real problems and solutions at start-ups, traditional financial services firms, and the VC and consulting communities which serve them.

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Sales and Business Development
classes.description: Sales and Business Development provides an overview of the principles and practices of direct sales and business development leveraging research, practical and experiential resources. Classes include instructor-driven content, expert practitioner guests, and experiential exercises. Participants will develop a go-to-market sales strategy for their startup projects as a final deliverable for the class.
classes.roster_syllabus_read: SP25 CURRENT (the SP26 file is a different course, AEM 4665)
classes.grading_summary: SP25 (real NBAY 5640): attendance 25, in-class cases/exercises 30, final sales presentation 45. SP26 file is a different course: plan 10, participation 50, presentation 40 points.

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Cryptocurrencies and Blockchains
classes.grading_summary: Homework 1 20, Homework 2 20, participation 25, comprehensive final exam 35

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Cybersecurity and Adversarial Thinking
classes.description: Overview: Think like an (ethical) hacker and get into the habit of asking, “How would I break this?” Students will learn the principles of secure system design by viewing systems as attackers do—probing assumptions, spotting attack surfaces, and reasoning about incentives, capabilities, and vulnerabilities. They will gain an appreciation for why cybersecurity matters in business and everyday life. Topics include user authentication, cryptography, malware, game-theoretic modeling, and privacy-enhancing technologies, with examples ranging from ordinary web use to cryptocurrency and AI. Prerequisites: No programming experience required. You must have basic data literacy (e.g., use of spreadsheets) and a willingness to experiment with modern tools (e.g., LLMs).
classes.grading_summary: HW1 10, HW2 10, participation plus quizzes 20, closed-book multiple-choice final 60

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Leading Through Complexity: Business Strategy for a Changing World
classes.description: The hardest business decisions rarely have a "right" answer. Leaders must balance growth with risk, innovation with responsibility, shareholder returns with broader stakeholder expectations and increasingly, opportunities and challenges created by emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. Drawing on the instructor's experience leading sustainability strategy at two leading financial institutions, this highly interactive, case-based course examines how executives, entrepreneurs, and investors navigate competing priorities. Through cases, guest speakers and class debate, students will explore how organizations create competitive advantage in a complex and rapidly changing business environment. The course is designed to prepare students to make thoughtful strategic decisions balancing financial, technological, environmental, and societal objectives.
classes.grading_summary: Participation 40, three team assignments 30 (10 each), final project 30

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Digital Marketing
classes.description: This course introduces students to fundamental concepts in digital marketing and prepares them for roles as a marketer, entrepreneur or product manager. Students will be exposed to an overview of the major players in the advertising and digital industries, as well as a variety of tools commonly found in start-ups and technology firms. Course material will be covered with a mixture of case studies, lectures, and guest speakers.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Master of Business Administration (MBA) students | Cornell Tech Master of Business Administration (MBA) students
classes.grading_summary: Participation 30, group project 30, take-home final 30, homework 10 (two at 5); extra credit up to 3 Google Ads certs at 1 each

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Core Leadership Skills for a VUCA World
classes.description: Core Leadership Skills for a VUCA World is designed to provide students with an opportunity to expand their knowledge and understanding of the key leadership skills required for success in today's volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous business world through discussion and interaction with an experienced practitioner and former leader of the United States Army. The course will be comprised of four modules: 1) Leadership Principles for a Volatile, Uncertain, Complex and Ambiguous World; 2) Developing and Communicating Vision and Strategy; 3) Setting Conditions for Success; and, 4) Character and Leadership. Coursework to include readings, discussion, and a final paper.
classes.grading_summary: Pass/fail: class participation 30, individual 2-page paper 70

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Business Models
classes.description: What does it take to make an idea or concept into a successful commercial undertaking? Well, a whole lot - a great product in a compelling market, a strong team with determination, and most certainly a sound business model. A business model defines how a company creates value with key resources and processes, how that value is delivered to customers, and ultimately how the company makes profits for shareholders. This course will cover different business model types as they evolve through a company's growth as well as the implications communicated via its financial models.
classes.grading_summary: Assignments 1-4 10 each, attendance and participation 20, final project 40

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Great Books V2.0: Lessons for Living and Leading in a Digital World
classes.description: This is a course modeled on a core curriculum comprising foundational texts that provide a comprehensive and shared base of knowledge that enables students to critically examine the role of technology, and by extension, their own role as leaders in the current social, economic, and political context. Like any 'Great Books' course, this course aims to prepare informed and active leaders for the greater good in the digital era. The books we will read in this seminar-style, discussion-based course are both cheerleaders and challengers of technology and business and the classroom discussions of the merits and demerits of the arguments in these books will help students learn about both the impact of technology on business and in society as well as how to mitigate the negative and augment the positive consequences. It will also build students' abilities to analyze topics and construct and articulate arguments.
classes.grading_summary: S/U; deliverables TBD, no single long final paper; mandatory attendance, one miss allowed

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Behavioral Economics in Decision Making
classes.description: This course on behavioral economics delves into its growing influence in business, particularly in product design, customer experiences, and managerial decision-making. Designed to cater to diverse student backgrounds and career goals, the course begins by exploring key theories and insights in behavioral economics. It then transitions to practical applications within business contexts. Emphasizing the applied application of behavioral economics insights, the course includes case studies for in-class discussion and hands-on projects like behavioral audits, A/B test design, and proposing behavioral solutions. It is particularly beneficial for students aspiring to careers in product development, data science, consulting, product marketing, or entrepreneurship.
classes.grading_summary: Three short assignments 45 (15 each), group final project 40, participation 15

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Ethical Decision Making in Management
classes.description: Poor moral judgment can ruin a manager's career or even sink a company. In general, an organization cannot survive without the trust of numerous stakeholders, and ethical lapses destroy trust and threaten vital stakeholder relationships. In today's volatile and fiercely competitive business environment, a manager must be able to identify and effectively resolve ethical issues that inevitably arise in the pursuit of business (and career) objectives. This course is designed to enhance students' skills in moral reasoning as it applies to managerial decision making. It thus examines normative concepts and principles that typically enter into moral reasoning and uses those concepts and principles in analyzing real-world cases. Discussions are designed to help students understand the moral issues confronting the decision makers in the cases and explore how those issues might be addressed in ethically responsible ways.

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Negotiation Essentials
classes.description: Negotiation is the art and science of securing an agreement between people who have some conflicting interests.Seen this way, you negotiate every day-with partners about travel plans, with roommates about dishwashing, with teammates about who writes the first draft of the paper. And you can begin to see how you can turn situations into profitable negotiations-getting a hotel room upgrade, managing a dispute on a client team, finagling a deadline extension.The goal of this class is to help you do better in these and other important negotiations. As is true in life, there is no formula you can simply apply to achieve success in negotiation. Nor is there a single right answer to the question of what is the best tactic to use. What we will do, however, is provide you with frameworks and empirical findings that shed light on which tactics are likely to be effective, given particular situational constraints (relationships, few outside options, etc.). Your jobs are to hone your ability to decide when a tactic is likely to work, and to practice using the appropriate skills to gain experience and confidence.

classes.subject: NBAY
classes.title: Machine Learning Applications in Business
classes.description: The purpose of this class is to introduce you to fundamental concepts in data science & machine learning (ML) and prepare you for your career path as an entrepreneur or various business roles (e.g. product manager, marketing, operations, consulting?etc) in for-profit & non-profit organizations. This course differs from the classes offered from the engineer side in that we will use a business-centric approach, where we first begin with the business problem to be solved, and then we cover the technical methodologies to solve the context-specific use cases. Throughout the course I will teach you a decision-making framework to unite the various disparate use cases under a common thread. This framework draws upon my years of experience as both an AI researcher and as a business consultant. I have been fortunate to apply ML to various business contexts, from Silicon Valley startups to the Fortune 500, from private equity to non-profit organizations, and I am actively using and evolving this framework in my current role as an entrepreneur in my own AI startup. I will show you how to use this framework using a mixture of business case studies, real-world context data sets, lectures, and guest speakers. My hope is that you will leave this course with the skills to assemble the talent/resources to tackle the data science and ML challenges that you will encounter when you work for large firms or starting your ventures.

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Discrete Optimization for Urban Planning and Mobility
classes.description: The course is organized around five major case studies on the use of discrete optimization and data (AI at large) for smart cities. Namely, 1) bike sharing, 2) bus transportation planning, 3) fairness in ambulance allocation (and police patrol), 4) downed tree reporting (NYC Department of Parks and Recreation), and 5) parcel delivery.The teaching is structured to provide three levels of understanding: a first level in which the problem is presented with its importance, impact, and characteristics. The need of a tech-based quantitative approach is claimed and justified. A second level in which, a high-level version of the algorithmic approach used to solve the problem is presented. A third level, dependent on students' interest and knowledge, in which the algorithmic approach is detailed.
classes.outcomes: Students will learn real case studies on modern city development, planning, and management. The three-level teaching structure should allow (i) the technically-oriented students to see how to use their competences on real-world problems, and (ii) the more domain-oriented students to be alerted at looking for technical solutions and recognize their need.
classes.prereq: basic knowledge of linear algebra and data management.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Designing and Running Personalized Health Experiments
classes.description: Traditionally, treatment guidelines and health recommendations are based on large cohort studies or randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which provide only average effect estimates. This limits their ability to predict whether an intervention will benefit an individual. With the rise of digital solutions, personalized approaches like N-of-1 trials are gaining traction. These modern designs allow for individual treatment effects and improve population-level effect estimates. This seminar covers N-of-1 trials and other modern study designs such as micro-randomized trials. First, we will get an overview of different study types and their characteristics, then we will give an introduction of the practical aspects for performing N-of-1 trials, and then the main focus of the class will be on methodological approaches for planning and analyzing N-of-1 trials.
classes.outcomes:
Understand the main concepts of planning & conducting N-of-1 trials and selected other study designs.
Perform individual-level and aggregated analysis of N-of-1 trials using state-of-the-art methods.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students
classes.grading_summary: Participation 20, paper presentation/moderation 30, final project presentation 20, final project report 30

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Distributed Optimization for Machine Learning and AI
classes.description: This is a graduate-level course about theory, algorithms and applications of distributed optimization and machine learning. The course covers the basics of distributed optimization and learning algorithms and their performance analyses when they are used to solve large-scale distributed problems arising in AI, machine learning, signal processing, communication networks, and power systems.
classes.outcomes:
Be able to formulate optimization problems arising from machine learning, signal processing, and wireless communication tasks.
Be able to implement numerically stable and scalable algorithms to solve practical optimization problems in large-scale learning and computing.
Be able to quantify convergence rates and resource efficiency of optimization algorithms in terms of iteration, computation and communication counts.
Be able to design, modify, and deploy optimization algorithms tailored to the structure and constraints of real-world learning and wireless computing systems. (For PhD students)
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students
classes.grading_summary: 5 homeworks 30, in-class exam 40, literature review 30 (5290 only; project replaces it for 7290)

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Reinforcement Learning with Operations Research Applications
classes.description: The ongoing information revolution and the advent of the big data era make quantitative methods in the business context indispensable. This course introduces reinforcement learning, decision-making under uncertainty, and related algorithms through the lens of OR applications. Examples will be drawn from real-world problems in operations, revenue management, queuing, finance, transportation, healthcare, and other areas of interest. The course will cover modeling and applications, basic theory, and algorithms.
classes.outcomes:
Be able to formalize dynamic decision problems under uncertainty as Markov decision processes.
Learn about finite-horizon and infinite-horizon MDPs.
Know how to solve MDPs exactly via dynamic programming as well as know how to solve MDPs approximately via reinforcement learning.
Learn to read the technical literature in operations research, machine learning, and control literature.
Gain hands-on experience in implementing and applying various exact and approximate algorithms.
classes.prereq: ORIE 3500 or ORIE 5500; ORIE 3510 or ORIE 5510; or equivalents.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students
classes.grading_summary: Problem sets 30 (7), lit review 25, methods/experiments 25, code 10, peer reviews 5, participation 5

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Applied Causal Inference using Machine Learning
classes.description: Provides an applied treatment of modern causal inference using machine learning to handle high-dimensionality and nonparametric estimation. Formulates key causal questions in the languages of structural equation modeling and potential outcomes. Presents methods for estimating and constructing confidence intervals on causal and structural parameters using machine learning, including de-biased machine learning, and for learning how to predict heterogeneous treatment effects. Introduces tools from machine learning and deep learning developed for prediction purposes and discusses how to adapt them to causal inference. Emphasizes the applied and practical perspectives with real-world-data examples and assignments. Requires basic knowledge of statistics and machine learning and programming experience in R or Python.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Computational Methods in Operations Research
classes.description: A suite of tools and techniques that enable computation in operations research. Structured and efficient programming, code optimization, code review, version management systems, building a user interface, exploring and manipulating large-scale datasets.
classes.prereq: background equivalent to: ENGRD 2700 and ORIE 3300.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: AI for Computational Research
classes.description: AI progress has, and will continue to, revolutionize scientific research. On tasks ranging from (some) theorem proving to coding experiments, they are superhuman. However, for much computational research, human researchers must remain in the loop to evaluate, guide, and steer AI, and we must understand its outputs in order to synthesize and effectively communicate with others. In this course, we will work together to develop skills for how to manage AI to help produce high-quality, trustworthy research. Specific modules – depending on individual student interest – will include verifying empirical analyses, theorem proving and autoformalization of math in Lean, coding architecture, qualitative research coding, and paper reviewing. A class project may include building tools and agent scaffolding to help others use AI in the research process. A core theme of the class will be how to develop and retain individual skills while using AI to complement one’s work, along with discussions of the values inherent in the scientific enterprise.
classes.outcomes:
Demonstrate ability to effectively use AI agents in research.
Identify tasks for which AI is appropriate and not appropriate.
Demonstrate ability to evaluate outputs and errors.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: LLMs for Better Decision-Making
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students
classes.grading_summary: In-class paper presentations 40, class participation 20, final project 40

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Selected Topics in Mathematical Programming
classes.description: Current research topics in mathematical programming.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Selected Topics in Applied Probability
classes.description: Topics are chosen from current literature and research areas of the staff.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students
classes.grading_summary: No weights; grades based on five homework assignments plus scribing 1-2 lecture notes

classes.subject: ORIE
classes.title: Selected Topics in Applied Statistics
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students
classes.grading_summary: FA26 (Yu): homework 40, project 40, participation 20; SP26 sections use 40/60 and 20/40/40 splits

classes.subject: REAL
classes.title: Real Estate Seminar Series
classes.description: Designed to bring students weekly into direct contact with real-estate professionals mainly through the use of videoconferences originating from locations around the world. (MHA-EL)

classes.subject: REAL
classes.title: Land Use Law
classes.description: This course will evaluate the means-formal/legal and informal/non-legal-by which landowners, developers, architects, planners, neighbors, private organizations, and government may shape the use of land in the United States.  Close attention will be paid to:  the tension between regulation and landowners' rights; aesthetic controls and historic preservation; planning concepts; constitutional issues; environmental concerns; and the role of markets.

classes.subject: REAL
classes.title: International Cases and Contracts
classes.description: This course investigates real estate transactions that originate outside the United States and may be in a foreign country, in which the motivations for deals and transactions are outside the norm.  These include informal financing techniques; deal structuring with several local and foreign constituents; the limitations of contracts; and bankruptcy, in Europe, the Middle East, East Asia, South Asia, and Africa.

classes.subject: REAL
classes.title: Special Topics in Real Estate
classes.description: This course addresses pertinent issues relative to real estate. Topics vary each semester. (MHA-EL)

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Impact Investing and Venture Capital Seminar
classes.description: Build ventures that are both investable and high-impact while thinking like an investor and designing like a founder. This intensive, four-session studio explores impact investing through diligence, venture selection, fundraising strategy, and fund design. Apply practical frameworks from philanthropy, venture capital, and public-sector investing; participate in a live investing simulation; and use community insights to strengthen product-market fit and assess risk. Open to technical, design, MBA, and other students, the seminar supports future founders, investors, operators, product leaders, public-sector technologists, and nonprofit builders. Sessions emphasize collaborative workshops, discussions, simulations, and case comparisons. Combining investor-style memos with founder-style sprints, students develop immediately usable tools for raising and allocating capital in mission-driven technology and integrating capital and policy into their work.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Attendance 20, participation 30, assignments and activities 30, final presentation 20 (percent)

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Early Adopters
classes.description: Explore and learn a set of methodologies that support identifying and onboarding early adopters as customers for a new product built at a startup company, corporation, or project that expects to reach large scale. Students will complete the class with a set of tools and examples of real contracts, frameworks, and system and process designs that can be used to help support them in acquiring their first customer. In addition to the tools to support customer acquisition, students will make an attempt at acquiring their first customer for a real or hypothetical startup that is being built in the Studio at Cornell Tech.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: No weights; attendance, participation, unspecified deliverables, and an exam on the last day

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Don't Sell Sand in the Desert
classes.description: This course will take you through a deep dive into identifying effective go-to-market strategies: how to pick the one(s) to test, how to implement, how to assess success, and how to pivot as necessary. The GTM strategy is the gateway to the future of your company's marketing and sales efforts and a misstep here can cost you time, money, or your business. We will pressure test every element and find the flaws now, not when you are already in the market. This course will include case studies, current real-world examples, lots of in-class teamwork and exercises, and guest lecturers with practical experience. We will work on your projects so that you can make real progress in this critical area.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Attendance 10, participation 10, assignments 30, final paper 25, final presentation 25

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Venture Capital Mindsets for Entrepreneurs
classes.description: Venture Capital Mindsets for Entrepreneurs is a tactical course for aspiring founders focused on how to identify, pitch to, and partner with the right investors. Students develop fluency in venture capital language and dynamics, gaining a practical understanding of how investors think and evaluate early-stage companies. The course culminates in a polished pitch presentation delivered to invited guests from the venture and startup community.
classes.outcomes:
Apply a venture capital mindset as an entrepreneur when evaluating funding paths and growth strategies.
Identify and assess potential investors based on alignment with a startup’s vision, stage, and goals.
Communicate effectively with investors using appropriate venture capital language and conventions.
Develop and deliver a professional pitch suitable for presentation to external stakeholders and investors.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Modeling New Ventures
classes.description: Every startup's financial model tells a story: how the founders believe the business works, what must be true for it to succeed, and what success looks like. In this course, students build an investor-grade model for their own early-stage tech venture, whatever its business model and even before revenue, and learn to read any model as an argument to be tested. Students leave able to tell their venture's story in numbers and defend it. No finance or accounting background required.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Digital Innovation in Retail
classes.description: This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of how retailers are enhancing their strategies to include innovative, and new-age technology (i.e. AR/VR, mobile, personalization, AI, etc.) to improve their branding and customer experience. The retail industry is increasingly competitive and rapidly evolving, and this course will explore the technical developments that are transforming the marketplace across multiple retail domains (i.e. CPG, grocery/superstores, fashion brands, department stores, technology retail businesses etc.). We will examine how the industry got to its current point, evaluate examples of newer technologies in practice (including their benefits and downfalls), and finally, explore the possible industry technological innovations for 2026.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Participation 40, final paper 30, attendance 10, four reading-prep assignments 5 each (percent)

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Building Legal Tech Ventures
classes.description: This course offers Cornell Tech students a broad overview of building a legaltech company from the founder perspective. Each week, a founder will join class to share how they developed a different functional area of their business, including product management, sales and marketing, and building the initial team. Through this course, students will gain an understanding of the opportunities and challenges of building a legaltech company and what specific roles may interest them within the legaltech ecosystem. They will also gain an appreciation for the strategic considerations and tactics necessary for building technology for legal professionals and consumers.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Product Management in the AI Era: Decision-Making for Entrepreneurs and Product Builders
classes.description:
Entrepreneurs and product managers must make consequential decisions quickly, often with incomplete information and competing priorities. This course builds the judgment, confidence, and adaptability needed to lead startups, products, and initiatives within established organizations. Through in-class exercises and team projects, students practice making and defending decisions about vision, strategy, design, product roadmaps, business models, metrics, go-to-market approaches, cross-functional leadership, and storytelling. Each topic explores key tradeoffs through practical frameworks, judgment, and product taste.
As new information emerges and constraints shift, teams revisit decisions, examine assumptions, assess alternatives, and adapt. Discussions and debriefs emphasize agency, experimentation, customer focus, and collaboration. Students learn to make thoughtful, timely decisions under pressure and clearly communicate their reasoning while responding to uncertainty and balancing competing priorities across teams and stakeholders.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Group assignments 30, personal reflections 30, peer critiques 20, professionalism and participation 20

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Branding for Products
classes.description: This course is designed to help students understand the strategic and practical aspects of designing a brand and an interface. We will cover the principles of brand strategy and brand design, user experience and interface design (UX/UI), and how to build a brand for the customer of the 21st century.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Onboarding survey 5, 2 assignments 15 each, participation 15, final project 40, peer feedback 10

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Research is a Team Sport
classes.description: Research is no longer only the researcher's job. As research decentralizes, PMs, designers, marketers, and engineers increasingly become people who do research. This course covers the fundamentals of research design, core methods, shaping insights, and building a narrative. Throughout, we'll discuss where AI helps—or gets in the way. Expect a collaborative, hands-on course: user interviews, survey design, and team critiques. It's designed for anyone who wants to influence product & business decisions with research.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Design for One
classes.description: Assistive technology is proof that a $25 microcontroller board can solve problems software can't — one-switch interfaces, reminder objects, sensory substitution — and "design for one, extend to many" is a storied design tradition (the OXO peeler started as a device for the founder's wife, who struggled with arthritic hands). Each student chooses one person they can actually reach — a grandparent, a roommate, themselves — observes one friction, and delivers a working, battery-powered device that addresses it. The no-internet constraint is the enabling constraint that enables: the device can't be discontinued, can't leak data, can't demand an update, and will still work in ten years. The course ends with a field-test story and a show and tell, and the object walks out of the room as a gift for the person it was built for.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Building AI Products
classes.description: This course provides a practical playbook for creating products powered by artificial intelligence and machine learning, including large language models (LLMs), agents, and multi-agent systems. Students explore the full product lifecycle, with particular emphasis on data and evaluations. Designed for anyone interested in AI products, the course welcomes aspiring product managers, startup founders, product attorneys, and students pursuing other roles. Diverse perspectives are valued, and no prior experience or expertise in machine learning, AI, LLMs, or agents is required. Any Cornell Tech student can succeed in the course. Some coding is involved, but students work in groups and are encouraged to use AI-assisted coding. The course offers an accessible foundation for contributing to AI product development across a range of professional paths.
classes.outcomes:
Demonstrate fundamental understanding of the baseline process for productizing machine learning.
Demonstrate the ability to critically adapt or revise the baseline process for productizing machine learning when applying it to a new target problem.
Demonstrate fundamental understanding of common industry tools and processes for productizing machine learning.
Demonstrate ability to thoughtfully map readings, lectures, and in-class comments and questions from classmates onto a new target problem chosen by student.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Group assignments 60, attendance 20, in-class analytical pieces 20, optional extra credit 10 (total 110)

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Crisis Management in Tech
classes.description: A crisis can strike at any time, and it can have major impacts on a business, its reputation, and its customers. This course prepares future tech industry leaders to navigate crises. Each session dives into real-world case studies encompassing data breaches, product failures, regulatory incidents, service disruptions, cybersecurity attacks, and more. Through in-depth analysis and practical applications, students explore the multifaceted landscape of tech crises, crafting actionable crisis management plans. This course arms participants with a comprehensive playbook, honing their abilities to mitigate risks, lead during crises, and learn from incidents, ensuring preparedness and resilience in the ever-evolving tech sphere.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Participation 20, HW1 postmortem 25, HW2 studio premortem 25, in-class crisis simulation final 30

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: Startup Studio
classes.description: Students cofound their own startups, developing their ideas, products, and pitches, learning to create and tell a compelling startup story, and test their product with users. Students participate in three 24-hour Maker Days where they focus on developing their product and final presentation at the end of the semester.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: BigCo Studio
classes.description: Most people who work in the tech industry will start and perhaps spend their careers in established companies. The companies-we call BigCos-have complex org structures, unique market dynamics, and different ways of getting things done. In this class, students will learn how to successfully navigate the opportunities and challenges of a BigCo and build products in a complex environment at scale from practitioners with extensive experience and prominent guest speakers. Students will also learn about how business development, M&A, and other corporate activities complement and sometimes compete with larger strategic initiatives. Students will work in teams matched with a real-world opportunity and advisor from a BigCo. Teams will build and pitch a product in three sprints culminating in a final presentation and demo.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: PiTech Impact Studio
classes.description: Nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and social ventures face unique challenges in developing digital products that serve under-resourced communities. These organizations must navigate complex stakeholder needs, limited resources, and mission-driven constraints. This course teaches students how to identify opportunities, prototype solutions, and validate digital products that advance public-interest missions. Students will work in teams matched with a real-world partner organization and advisor, applying skills in AI, data science, and human-centered design to challenges spanning public health, food security, family support, gender-based violence, education and career readiness, and housing stability. Teams will build and pitch a product in three sprints, culminating in a final presentation and demo.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: non-first year Jacobs Cornell Tech Master's students
classes.grading_summary: Project deliverables 70, presentations 15, class participation 15; three equal Maker Days

classes.subject: TECH
classes.title: DeployAI Studio
classes.description: AI can do a great deal, yet most organizations have changed little in how they work. This course teaches a structured approach to deploying AI and applies it in a semester-long project with a partner organization: a small company, nonprofit, Cornell department, or large company. Students learn to assess where AI can do an organization’s work and to design a complete initiative, including the opportunity, the technical architecture, and changes to jobs, metrics, and incentives. Each initiative is then tested through screening, economic analysis, low-cost experiments, and field validation. Teams build a working system, measure whether it handles the partner’s real work reliably, and prepare it for ongoing operation. The course mixes instruction with team working sessions.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech Master's students except first year Jacobs students

classes.subject: TECHIE
classes.title: Law for Non-Lawyers
classes.description: This class introduces the principal legal issues involved in starting, managing and operating a technology-oriented business by entrepreneurs. It is intended to provide non-law students with an understanding of many of the laws and regulations to which developing businesses in the United States tech sector are typically subject-from the time an entrepreneur conceives and begins to build a business, implements a business plan, and obtains financing, to when she begins operations in anticipation of managing a mature company and considering possible exit strategies.The instructor, a former corporate partner in a large New York City law firm, will adopt the role of a general counsel to a start-up company advising his client/students about how laws and regulations affect their businesses at various stages of development, as well as about typical key contractual terms and negotiating strategies. Practicing lawyers specializing in areas of the law-tax, intellectual property, employment law and others particularly relevant to start-up technology companies-will serve as guest lecturers.The course is designed to impart an understanding not only about substantive areas of the law that intersect with tech businesses but also about the role that lawyers should-and should not -play in burgeoning business enterprises. Students will gain insights into how lawyers approach business problems and the benefits and limitations of such a perspective.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students
classes.grading_summary: Pass/fail; one open-book take-home final exam; mandatory attendance; no percentage weights

classes.subject: TECHIE
classes.title: Building Agentic Systems
classes.description: In this course we will engage in the art and science of orchestrating modern software systems, positioning students as producers rather than just coders. Participants will learn to define product scope, translate high-level vision into rapid, iterative deliverables, and manage the full lifecycle of a technology “production” by leveraging contemporary developer ecosystems, cloud services, and data pipelines. Through a blend of lectures and working sessions, students will explore the architectural, operational, and collaborative parts of building technology systems that meet real-world application needs. By the end of the term, each student will have produced several tangible software artifacts demonstrating familiarity with both the technical and managerial aspects of modern and emerging technology production. This course is geared for Jacobs students and Cornell Tech students without a technical background.
classes.enrollment_limited_to: Cornell Tech students
classes.grading_summary: Attendance 30, quizzes 30, working sessions 40 (percent); weekly Wednesday quiz and working session 10 points each

# Mohamed Abdelfattah
Reference data compiled 2026-10-19 from public sources; follow-up searches completed 2026-10-24; not interview evidence.

## At a glance
- Appointment / title: Assistant Professor
- School, department or program: Electrical and Computer Engineering, Cornell Engineering and Cornell Tech; also CSL
- Expertise / research areas: ML-hardware co-design, efficient LLMs, AutoML and network compression, new ML hardware architectures, FPGAs and reconfigurable computing
- Career and industry background: Intel programmable solutions group; Samsung (led a team on hardware-aware AutoML); cofounder and Chief Scientific Officer of Makora (GPU efficiency startup, 2025)
- Education (if public): B.Sc. German University in Cairo; M.Sc. Stuttgart; Ph.D. Toronto (Vanier scholar)
- Teaches in SP27: CS 5775 / ECE 5545 Machine Learning Hardware and Systems (Cornell Tech)
- Taught at Cornell Tech before (roster): SP25 and SP26 CS 5775 and ECE 5545

## Bio
Mohamed Abdelfattah designs the hardware and software stack that makes neural networks, especially large language models, run efficiently. After industry roles at Intel and Samsung they joined Cornell Tech. They run a research group, linked from their site, and have co-founded a startup.

## Networking angle
- Cofounder/CSO of Makora; the Cornell Tech page spells it "Mako", the personal site "Makora".
- Awards listed: NSF CAREER (Jan 2024), Meta Research Award in Networking for AI (2022), best paper at AutoML 2024.
- Group site (abdelfattah-lab.github.io) has a Team page; the personal site lists no prospective student information.
- Relevant to students in ML systems and chips; related to De Sa's ML systems work.

## Links
- Official profile: https://www.tech.cornell.edu/people/mohamed-abdelfattah/
- Personal / lab / company site: http://www.mohsaied.com/ ; group site https://abdelfattah-lab.github.io/ (fetched 2026-10-24: Abdelfattah Research Group, Cornell Tech; themes: deep neural network compression, efficient AI systems for hosting and sharding LLMs, hardware/software codesign, reconfigurable computing; 16 current members, 15 alumni; publications at /pubs; no Scholar link on the site)
- Scholar / other: Cornell CS profile https://www.cs.cornell.edu/people/mohamed-abdelfattah
- Public contact as listed on official page: mohamed@cornell.edu

## Confidence and gaps
Identity: confirmed. Not fetched: group site, Google Scholar, company site. Search budget ran out partway through the batch. Follow-up 2026-10-24: group site read; it names no startup, so the Mako/Makora spelling remains unverified (the Cornell Tech profile is the only source). Scholar page not fetched (not linked from the group site).

## At a glance
- Appointment / title: Eleanora and George Landew Professor of Management; Professor of Management and Organizations
- School, department or program: Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management (Cornell SC Johnson College of Business); listed as Studio faculty at Cornell Tech; CV office listed at Cornell Tech (Tata)
- Expertise / research areas: Innovation, technology commercialization, interfirm collaboration and networks, strategy and competitive analysis, alliances and acquisitions
- Career and industry background: Primarily academic; previously University of Michigan Ross School (2001-2017), UT Austin (1996-2001), visiting at Harvard Business School (2014-2015); former editor-in-chief of Organization Science. No ventures found
- Education (if public): PhD (corporate strategy), MA and MBA, University of Michigan; PGDM, Indian Institute of Management; BA economics, St. Stephen's College, Delhi
- Teaches in SP27: TECH 5920 BigCo Studio (Cornell Tech)

## Bio
Gautam Ahuja is a strategy and innovation scholar who joined Cornell in 2017 and teaches strategy and competitive analysis. At Cornell Tech, Ahuja teaches BigCo Studio, a course where student teams build and pitch a product to a large company, each paired with a company advisor at VP or C-suite level.

## Networking angle
- BigCo Studio connects teams to a senior advisor at a large company: a route to corporate contacts (course description; Product Studio is a prerequisite).
- Research on alliances, acquisitions and technology commercialization suits corporate-partnership and corporate-innovation interests.
- Listed on Cornell Tech's Studio faculty page.

- Personal / lab / company site: not located

## At a glance
- Appointment / title: Professor
- School, department or program: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Cornell Engineering

Reference data compiled 2026-10-19 from public sources; follow-up searches completed 2026-10-24; not interview evidence.

- Appointment / title: Associate Professor of Population Health Sciences (Division of Health Informatics), Weill Cornell Medicine. The Cornell Bowers page shows conflicting ranks (Assistant in the header, Associate in the bio); the Weill news item says Associate.
- School, department or program: Weill Cornell Medicine (NYC); field faculty in Computer Science and Information Science, field member in Statistics (Cornell Bowers)

Wang directs the Institute of AI for Digital Health at Weill Cornell Medicine and works on applying machine learning to clinical and health data.
